item.title: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns
item.description: As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.

item.title: New York City unveils a bold plan to move its jails off Rikers Island
item.description: New York City officials are moving forward with plans to close Rikers, the city's main jail complex, after years of discussion. The jail has been plagued by assaults and inmate deaths.

item.title: The U.K. and EU hold a rare summit to strengthen ties
item.description: A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences.

item.title: How non-player characters in 'Grand Theft Auto VI' help create its big world
item.description: In video games, "barks" are short lines of dialogue given to various characters in the world. Grand Theft Auto VI proves how this kind of dialogue contributes to an immersive world.

item.title: Why the U.S. air traffic control system still relies on an 'antique' network
item.description: The FAA says the telecom outage that led to Friday's nationwide ground stop began with an upgrade to fiber-optic cables. Industry experts say the work is long overdue.

item.title: How the Steadicam sprinted up the stairs along with Rocky
item.description: A new movie about the making of Sylvester Stallone's 1976 film Rocky opens nationwide this week. It made him a star and helped revolutionize cinematography — including technology still used today.
